text.p: Portuguese bonds firmed in quiet trade and dealers said shorter maturities had strong support and 10-year bonds would follow their Spanish equivalents.
"Although liquidity is low, the market is firm and if Spain makes gains prices will rise here too," said one trader.
"I don't think there will be a big change in spreads against German Bunds. We're going to track Spain," another dealer said.
"There may be some profit-taking but this can easily be absorbed since there is still a conviction that we will push higher," he said.

Dealers said a growing belief that Portugal would enter the European Union's single currency in the first wave of countries was supporting prices but there would only be a strong rise if convergence was confirmed.
Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa told a Lisbon newspaper today that Portugal was well-placed to join the euro from the outset in 1999.
Money market rates were little changed in quiet trade. Overnight/tomorrow next rates were quoted at 6.77/6.80 percent after 6.75/6.85 yesterday.
